A copper-red acorn cap tub straining under a veined ivy-leaf sail, a lean split-acorn rowed hard by a fae with amber hair flat along the thwart, a plum-dark pea-pod skiff poled off a grey river-pebble standing over the fleet like a cliff, a cream hazelnut shell towed on a grass line by a harnessed dragonfly zigzagging ahead, and a scarlet rose-petal coracle spinning helplessly between them all — its fae kneeling and laughing.

Five hulls in a knot at the twig-arch gate: a moss-green walnut shell rowed with split-reed oars, a marigold birch-bark curl under a moth-wing sail showing one dark eyespot, a fat berry-red acorn cap shipping water over its rim, a long ivory seed-pod with a pointed bow paddled by a fae leaning far out, and a bracket-fungus raft that has somehow taken the lead, its fae poling with both feet braced, a fallen oak leaf drifting past as wide as all five hulls together.

A deep cobalt-painted hazelnut shell under a scarlet poppy petal with one painted crescent, a tubby copper acorn cap rowed with flat-seed oars, a lean plum pea-pod skiff towed by a harnessed dragonfly on a grass cord that keeps snapping taut, a pale birch-bark curl poled off a mossy stone, and a twin-reed outrigger in bright amber lashed with grass cord skimming the outside of the bend — the charm: a single snail on the bank keeping easy pace with them all.

A fat cream walnut shell under a broad marigold petal sail with its own dark nectar streak, a copper-brown seed-pod with pointed bow rowed by a fae with chestnut hair, a scarlet folded-oak-leaf punt riding high, a long lean hollow-reed hull paddled hard, and a plum-dark snail-shell boat corkscrewing as it goes — a watercress strand crossing the channel ahead of the fleet like a low green bridge everyone must duck beneath.

Six hulls bunched at the bulrush-stem start: a berry-red acorn cap with a twig mast and a fan of birch bark for a sail carrying its own dark lenticel dashes, a lean ivory pea-pod skiff, a flat bracket-fungus raft poled by two tiny palm-sized fae in woven-grass tunics, a moss-green hazelnut shell rowed hard, a twin-reed catamaran in amber, and a deep plum magnolia-leaf punt whose fae has tied a spare dandelion-down sail to the bow in case the first one tears.

A turquoise acorn cap tub hard on the heels of a lean scarlet birch-bark curl; behind them a fat cream walnut shell under a faded-gold petal sail, a long amber reed hull paddled by a fae with dark braided hair lying flat, and a chestnut-spiny seed-pod rounding a rowanberry gate with its keel-pebble showing through the clear water like a dropped coin — a mayfly hovering at eye level, its wings as wide as the reed hull is long.

A moss-green pea-pod skiff poled fast, a plum rose-petal coracle spinning backward through the gate, a lean copper birch-bark curl under a veined hornbeam-leaf sail, a fat ivory acorn cap rowed with two flat seeds held in wing-thin fae hands, and a bracket-fungus raft in umber shipping a tiny wave that slops over its bow — the charm: the fae aboard the bracket-fungus raft bailing with a single acorn cap, expression murderous.

A scarlet hazelnut shell under a whole white clover-flower for a sail, a lean twin-reed outrigger in honey-gold lashed with plaited grass, a tubby plum walnut shell rowed with split reeds, a long pale seed-pod skimming fast under a moth-wing sail showing one painted spiral, and a deep copper folded-oak-leaf punt whose fae has stood upright to pole — a bulrush rising behind the fleet taller than any mast, dwarfing every sail at once.

A fat amber acorn cap tub towed by a harnessed dragonfly on a fraying grass cord, a lean berry-red birch-bark skiff rowed with split-reed oars, a cream magnolia-leaf punt curled at both ends under a broad scarlet petal, a plum-dark snail-shell boat with a pebble keel, and a moss-green bracket-fungus raft poled by a fae with copper-red hair — the raft's pebble-ballast has rolled to one end and the whole thing tips at a comedic angle.

A deep scarlet walnut shell under a pansy-petal sail with one small painted dot at its centre, a long ivory hollow-reed hull paddled by a fae in petal-silk the colour of new leaves, a fat plum acorn cap rowed hard into the bend, a thin copper seed-pod with a pointed bow skimming outside the pack, and a twin-reed catamaran in moss-green whose crossbar lashing has half unravelled — a single fern frond overhanging the whole field like a green roof, darkening every sail beneath it.

Five hulls in a spray-kicking line: a copper-brown acorn cap under a scarlet petal sail, a lean plum birch-bark curl towed by a harnessed dragonfly whose thread of grass cord hums taut, a fat cream hazelnut shell rowed with flat-seed paddles, a long amber pea-pod skiff with a pointed bow, and a folded-hornbeam-leaf punt in moss-green that has taken the inside of every gate and leads by a boat-length — the charm: a beetle gripping the punt's stem with all six legs, silent ballast.

A tubby marigold walnut shell under a white moth-wing sail showing one dark eyespot, a long scarlet hollow-reed hull poled fast, a moss-green acorn cap rowed with split reeds, a lean plum birch-bark skiff under a veined oak-leaf sail, a fat ivory bracket-fungus raft poled by two palm-sized fae in leaf-cloth, and a copper seed-pod trailing a grass-cord wake — one river pebble on the streambed below them looking, from fae height, like a submerged grey hill.

A deep plum snail-shell boat corkscrewing through the rowanberry gate, a lean scarlet pea-pod skiff paddled hard on the outside, a fat cream acorn cap whose twig mast has snapped and now drags sideways under a half-collapsed ivy-leaf sail, a copper birch-bark curl under a marigold petal, and a moss-green twin-reed outrigger harnessed to a dragonfly that veers left and right, changing its mind twice a second — the charm: the dragonfly's rider shrieking instructions the dragonfly ignores.

A broad amber bracket-fungus raft poled by a fae with a grass-cord sash and dark eyes, a scarlet rose-petal coracle spinning but somehow advancing, a lean ivory hollow-reed hull rowed with split-reed oars, a deep plum walnut shell under a hornbeam-leaf sail showing its branching silver veins, and a copper seed-pod with pointed bow and a painted crescent on its side — a fallen oak leaf drifting past them all as wide as three hulls end to end.

Six hulls at the dandelion-down garland: a fat moss-green acorn cap first through, a lean plum birch-bark curl second under a scarlet petal gust-lifted and pulling hard, a cream hazelnut shell rowed hard in third, a deep copper pea-pod skiff fourth, a twin-reed catamaran in marigold towed by a dragonfly in fifth, and a flat ivory bracket-fungus raft last and slow — the charm: the dandelion-down garland has stuck to the acorn cap's mast and streams behind it like a comet tail.

A berry-red walnut shell rowed with split reeds by a fae with amber braids, a long lean seed-pod in pale cream under a broad marigold petal sail, a fat copper acorn cap tipping dangerously as its fae leans far out to push off a pebble, a moss-green magnolia-leaf punt poled steady, and a plum rose-petal coracle with a single smooth river-pebble keel — a mayfly hanging in the air beside the coracle, its veined wings as wide as the coracle's beam.

A lean scarlet hollow-reed hull paddled flat out, a tubby plum acorn cap under a cream clover-flower sail, a copper birch-bark curl whose fae is poling off a grain-of-sand boulder with a split-reed staff, a fat ivory walnut shell towed by a harnessed dragonfly on a plaited grass line, and a deep moss-green seed-pod with a pointed bow and a moth-wing sail with one painted spiral — a watercress strand crossing the channel ahead, green and low, and the reed hull going under it without slowing.

A fat marigold acorn cap rowed hard, a long plum pea-pod skiff towed by a dragonfly on a grass cord, a deep scarlet walnut shell under a broad white petal with one small painted sprig of three dots, a copper twin-reed outrigger with its float skipping off every ripple, a cream birch-bark curl with dark lenticel dashes running the length of her side, and a moss-green bracket-fungus raft flat and slow at the back — the charm: a water-vole swimming behind the raft, convinced it is a passing island.

A deep copper hazelnut shell under a plum-purple poppy petal, a lean scarlet birch-bark skiff paddled by a fae with green-leaf leggings lying flat along the hull, a fat cream acorn cap rowed with flat-seed oars, a long amber reed hull poled fast through the gate, and a folded hornbeam-leaf punt in moss-green towing a tiny walnut-shell tender with a mouse asleep inside it — a bulrush rising on the bank taller than all five masts stacked, casting a stripe of shadow across the whole fleet.

A scarlet rose-petal coracle spinning through the first twig-arch gate, a lean ivory seed-pod with a pointed bow hard behind it, a fat plum walnut shell under a veined ivy-leaf sail, a moss-green acorn cap whose pebble keel has swung loose and clunks side to side, and a copper birch-bark curl towed by a harnessed dragonfly that has decided to fly upward — hull dangling, fae dangling, everyone watching — a fern frond above the whole scene making a low vaulted ceiling of green.

A long amber pea-pod skiff under a scarlet petal sail with one painted crescent, a fat cream walnut shell rowed with split reeds, a moss-green acorn cap poled by a fae in grass-woven sandals, a plum-dark hollow-reed hull paddled fast on the outside bend, and a copper twin-reed catamaran towed by a dragonfly whose harnessing grass cord is looped twice round the helmfae's wrist by accident — the catamaran slewing sideways, the dragonfly unperturbed, the fae furious.

Five hulls in a tight cluster under a fern frond that roofs them all: a deep scarlet magnolia-leaf punt curled at the bow, a lean copper birch-bark curl under a moth-wing sail showing one dark eyespot, a tubby marigold acorn cap rowed hard with flat-seed paddles, a plum snail-shell boat corkscrewing left, and a pale cream seed-pod with a pointed bow and a pebble keel glinting through the water — the charm: the snail-shell boat is actually gaining on the corkcrew.

A copper walnut shell flat-spinning around a rowanberry tethered at the gate on a grass cord, a lean scarlet hollow-reed hull paddled hard, a fat plum acorn cap under a broad white petal with one painted dot, a cream birch-bark curl with a fan-sail of dark-dashed bark, and a moss-green bracket-fungus raft poled by a wide-eyed fae with reed-fibre hair — a single river pebble on the bed below them casting a shadow that swallows two hulls at once.

A plum-dark pea-pod skiff towed by a harnessed dragonfly too fast for comfort, a scarlet acorn cap rowed hard at an angle into the gate, a lean cream birch-bark curl under a marigold petal sail, a fat moss-green walnut shell whose twig mast is held upright by the fae's left hand alone, and a deep amber seed-pod with a pointed bow paddled by a fae flat along the hull — a single mayfly lifting off the water beside the pea-pod, wings as wide as the hull is tall.

A fat copper acorn cap under a plum-dark pansy petal with its own gold thread of natural colour, a long lean ivory hollow-reed hull rowed by a fae with chestnut hair and both ears visible and pointed, a moss-green magnolia-leaf punt poled steady amidships, a scarlet hazelnut shell towed by a dragonfly on a looped grass cord, and a twin-reed outrigger in amber skimming fastest of all — the charm: a loose dandelion seed from the garland at the finish has blown back and lodged in the amber outrigger's bow like an uninvited passenger.
